value.query: How Chrome extensions, DevTools CDP, PWAs and WebGPU interact with an embedded Chromium browser

content.text:
### chrome.appviewTag.connect()

Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/apps/reference/appviewTag

Requests another app to be embedded into the current Chrome App.

```APIDOC
## chrome.appviewTag.connect()

### Description
Requests another app to be embedded. Returns a Promise that resolves to a boolean indicating success.

### Syntax
`chrome.appviewTag.connect(app: string, data?: any, callback?: function): Promise<boolean>`

### Parameters
- **app** (string) - Required - The extension id of the app to be embedded.
- **data** (any) - Optional - Optional developer specified data that the app to be embedded can use when making an embedding decision.
- **callback** (function) - Optional - A callback function that receives a boolean indicating if the embedding request succeeded.

### Returns
- **Promise<boolean>** - A promise that resolves to true if the embedding request succeeded.
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Chrome DevTools MCP Server

Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/ai/build-with-ai

Add this configuration to your MCP server settings to enable extension tools and automatic profile connection.

```json
{
 "mcpServers": {
   "chrome-devtools-mcp": {
     "args": [
       "-y",
       "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest",
       "--categoryExtensions",
       "--autoConnect"
     ],
     "command": "npx"
   }
 }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Forward CDP socket to local port

Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/remote-debugging

Maps the remote Chrome DevTools Protocol socket on the Android device to a local port on the development machine.

```bash
adb forward tcp:9222 localabstract:chrome_devtools_remote
```

### Concepts and usage > Targets

Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/debugger

The chrome.debugger API allows extensions to send Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) commands to specific targets, such as tabs, iframes, or workers. Each target is identified by a unique UUID and type. Within a single target, multiple execution contexts may exist, particularly for same-process iframes.

--------------------------------

### WebGPU > Prerequisite

Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/webgpu/developer-features

Chrome provides specific WebGPU features designed exclusively for development and testing that fall outside the standard WebGPU specification. These features should never be used in production environments. To access them, users must enable the WebGPU Developer Features flag in Chrome and restart the browser.
